title: Family Threat Picture — St. Louis Metro East
location: St. Clair County, IL (St. Louis Metro East)

overall.summary: Overall: Elevated, unchanged. US-Iran/Hormuz stays the top threat (High, Rising): two tanker strikes were reported near Oman's Khasab Saturday and Iran says a tanker hit a mine, while Iran's convoy talk continues. Taiwan reported 21 Chinese aircraft in a 'joint readiness patrol' (trend now Rising). Poland asked NATO for more air defense but did not invoke Article 4 (NATO trend back to Steady). Locally Guarded: no NWS alerts, one more warm day (72), light rain Sunday, then 27-28 degree lows Monday-Tuesday nights. Air quality improved to AQI 57, river 4.4 ft and falling, almost no outages, gas $3.84 locally.
overall.watchItem: Whether more tankers are hit or an Iranian convoy sails; China's readiness patrols around Taiwan; market open Monday; first hard freeze Monday night.

whatChanged.title: Tankers hit near Hormuz
whatChanged.detail: UKMTO: two projectile strikes on tankers near Khasab, Oman; Iran says a tanker hit a mine. No casualties. Iran stays High, Rising.

whatChanged.title: China readiness patrol near Taiwan
whatChanged.detail: Taiwan MND: 21 PLA aircraft sorties, 15 across the median line, with ships. Taiwan trend Steady to Rising.

whatChanged.title: Poland holds off on Article 4
whatChanged.detail: Warsaw asked for more NATO AWACS and F-35s instead; Rutte visiting. NATO trend Rising to Steady.

whatChanged.title: More Russian strikes on Ukraine
whatChanged.detail: 148 drones and 3 ballistic missiles overnight; 2 killed in Kryvyi Rih; power plant and substation hit. Ukraine stays Elevated, Rising.

whatChanged.title: Air quality better, gas cheaper
whatChanged.detail: AQI 86 to 57 (Moderate, trend Falling). AAA East St. Louis regular $3.84 (from $3.87). River 4.4 ft and falling.

topActions.title: Finish winterizing today
topActions.detail: Today (72 and sunny) is the last warm day: disconnect hoses, cover outdoor faucets, check the furnace and CO alarms, and stage winter car kits. Light rain Sunday, then lows 27-28 Monday and Tuesday nights.

topActions.title: Keep cash, fuel and staples buffers
topActions.detail: Tanker strikes near Hormuz and Monday's market open are the risks to watch: keep some cash, top off fuel while it's cheaper ($3.84 East St. Louis) and keep a few weeks of staples. No panic moves.

topActions.title: Flu shots and MMR check before Thanksgiving
topActions.detail: Flu is rising early and measles is spreading nationally: get flu shots now and confirm two MMR doses for everyone before holiday travel.

threats.name: US–Iran war and Strait of Hormuz
threats.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported two tanker incidents near Oman's Khasab at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 21: an outbound tanker hit in the stern by an unidentified projectile 11 nm north of Khasab, and a tanker hit in the engine room 17 nm east; no casualties (CNBC/Reuters, Nov 21). Iran's navy says a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted zone east of the strait; Reuters could not verify that. An Iranian lawmaker says 14 tankers are preparing to break the US blockade, but no official convoy has been announced (Iran International, Nov 21). UKMTO says Hormuz traffic was about 65% below pre-war levels in the week to Nov 18. Brent settled $92.57 Nov 20. Level High, trend Rising.
actions: Keep 2+ weeks of water, food, prescriptions and fuel on hand; rotate, don't panic-buy.
A clash between the tanker convoy and US ships, or a confirmed attack on US forces, would raise this to Severe.
Keep a battery/crank radio and charged power banks; know your NOAA Weather Radio frequency.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Russia–NATO tension and nuclear rhetoric
threats.summary: After two Russian missiles (one a confirmed Kh-101) and a jet drone came down in southeastern Poland on Nov 20, Warsaw asked NATO for more AWACS and F-35s under Operation Eastern Sentry but has stopped short of invoking Article 4 (Al Jazeera, Nov 21). NATO Secretary General Rutte called it a 'grave violation' and is expected in Poland this weekend. No injuries or damage; no Article 5 step. Level Elevated, trend Steady (was Rising).
actions: Know your shelter-in-place spot: basement center, away from windows.
Keep a battery or hand-crank NOAA radio and spare batteries.
Verify any nuclear alert through two official sources before acting (see fake-alert item).
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Russia–Ukraine war
threats.summary: Overnight Nov 20-21 Russia launched 3 ballistic missiles and 148 drones; Ukraine downed or jammed 117 drones, with hits at 19 locations (Ukraine Air Force via Kyiv Independent, Nov 21). Strikes on Kryvyi Rih killed 2, including a 7-year-old, and injured 58-83 across Ukraine; Russia says it hit the Kryvyi Rih thermal power plant and a Rivne substation. This follows the Nov 20 mass strike (400+ drones, 110+ missiles) that forced emergency power outages in 11 regions. Level Elevated, trend Rising.
actions: No direct family action; watch the date of the next round of talks.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: China–Taiwan pressure
threats.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry said Nov 21 (12:10 PM Taiwan time) that from 8:46 AM it detected 21 Chinese military aircraft sorties (J-10, J-16, Su-30, H-6K bombers, KJ-500, YY-20 tankers, drones), 15 of them crossing the median line into central and southwestern airspace, together with PLA ships in a so-called 'joint combat readiness patrol'. That is up from 8 sorties in the previous daily report. Level Elevated, trend Rising (was Steady).
actions: A Taiwan blockade would hit electronics and medicines first: keep 60–90 days of critical prescriptions where insurance allows.
Replace aging phones, radios, or chargers you rely on before shortages, not after.
threats.label: official

threats.name: North Korea
threats.summary: No confirmed new North Korean launch found when checked Nov 21; a Nov 17 launch claim seen on a minor site was not confirmed by Yonhap's Nov 17 summary. Last confirmed: Nov 4, when Seoul said several missiles flew toward the East Sea (Yonhap). Level Guarded, Steady.
actions: Monitor only; no family action needed now.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Fake emergency alerts
threats.summary: No new incidents found through Nov 9. On Nov 1 hackers took over Ukraine's Air Alert app and Russia's EMERCOM app and sent fake nuclear, radiation and chemical warnings; both were shut down or restored, and official siren, SMS, TV and radio systems were unaffected. (Carried over from earlier briefs; not rechecked this run.)
actions: Agree as a family: confirm any major alert on NOAA radio, weather.gov, or local TV before acting.
Rely on Wireless Emergency Alerts and NWS for official warnings; treat third-party app alerts as unverified.
threats.label: assessment

threats.name: Terrorism (DHS NTAS)
threats.summary: DHS NTAS shows no current advisories (checked Nov 21 morning). In the Peoria, Illinois ethanol-plant explosive-device case, a suspect has been indicted (WCBU, Nov 17); no new regional threat reported. Level Guarded, Steady.
actions: Normal awareness at crowded events; agree on a family rally point if separated.
Report suspicious packages near plants, rail yards or pipelines to police (See Something, Say Something).
threats.label: official

threats.name: Cyber threats to infrastructure
threats.summary: USDA's farm-payment outage was a 'cyberthreat,' a USDA under secretary said; NBC News (Nov 20) reports outside hackers accessed the farmer-payment system. USDA says no data was lost and most systems should be back by end of Friday, with weekend work if not; no restoration confirmation or CISA statement found as of Nov 21. CISA added four exploited vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog Nov 20 (VMware vCenter auth bypass, Cisco Expressway hard-coded credentials, SAP NetWeaver, Apache Roller); 15 added in the last 14 days. Level Elevated, trend Rising.
actions: Update home routers, phones and any Synology NAS now; don't expose a NAS to the internet.
Keep some cash and a few days of essentials in case card, bank or travel systems go down again.
Use a password manager and app-based two-factor on email and banking.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Measles (US)
threats.summary: CDC's Nov 19 update: 5,838 confirmed US measles cases in 2026, up 426 in one week, the largest weekly jump in decades and the 15th straight triple-digit week; 96% of cases are unvaccinated or unknown status (CIDRAP, Nov 20). Big outbreaks in Pennsylvania (1,631), Wisconsin (832), Indiana (227) and Minnesota (203). This follows the Nov 17 loss of US elimination status. Level Elevated, trend Rising.
actions: Confirm everyone in the household has two MMR doses on record (97% effective).
Check the IDPH page for Metro East exposure sites.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Seasonal flu and H5 bird flu
threats.summary: CDC FluView week 45 (ending Nov 14, posted Nov 20): seasonal flu keeps rising nationally and many indicators are higher than usual for mid-November, mostly A(H1N1); severity so far rated low. Two more pediatric deaths (7 this season). One new human H5 bird-flu case in an Oregon dairy worker (eye irritation; no human-to-human spread in the US). Week 46 report comes Nov 30 due to Thanksgiving. Level Elevated, trend Rising.
actions: Get flu shots for everyone now (CDC recommends now).
Stock a sick-room kit: thermometer, fever reducer, electrolytes, masks.
Antivirals work best started early; call the doctor on day one of symptoms.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Ebola (Bundibugyo), DR Congo
threats.summary: WHO Africa's Nov 15 report: 11,432 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases and 5,593 deaths in DR Congo across 68 health zones, with 442 new cases in the week of Nov 9-15. WHO's emergency committee met for the third time Nov 17. Spread has slowed in early hotspots but 400-500 cases a week continue. No US cases. Level Low for the US, Steady.
actions: No family action unless traveling to Central Africa.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Melioidosis (soil bacterium B. pseudomallei) in the U.S. Gulf Coast
threats.summary: UC Davis Health (Nov 6) reports the tropical soil and water bacterium Burkholderia pseudomallei may be slowly establishing in new regions including the U.S.; CDC says it is found on Mississippi's Gulf Coast, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and most U.S. cases are in travelers. Rare, treatable with antibiotics, easily mistaken for other illnesses; caught from contaminated soil, dust or water, very rarely person to person. Rechecked Nov 9: no CDC, IDPH or MO DHSS report of the bacterium or a locally acquired case in Illinois or Missouri found; no new UC Davis item. CDC weekly notifiable-disease tables (compiled by ENCLAI) show 4 U.S. cases in 2026 through Oct 25.
actions: No action needed in the St. Louis area now; the bacterium has not been reported in Illinois or Missouri.
When gardening, digging or doing storm cleanup (especially on Gulf Coast trips), wear waterproof boots and gloves, and a well-fitting N95 in dusty soil or after heavy rain or flooding.
Keep cuts and scrapes clean and covered; avoid soil and standing floodwater with open wounds, diabetes, kidney or liver disease, or heavy alcohol use (CDC risk factors).
Don't drink untreated water; boil or treat it when traveling or camping.

After a trip to the Gulf Coast, Puerto Rico, Southeast Asia or northern Australia, tell a doctor about the travel if you get fever, cough, chest or stomach pain, a sore that won't heal, confusion or seizures.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Economy, fuel, supply chain
threats.summary: Markets closed for the weekend after Nov 20, when the S&P 500 (-3.7%) and Dow entered correction and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026 (CNBC, Nov 20). Brent settled $92.57 Nov 20, down 3.4% on the week. Fuel keeps easing: AAA Nov 21 Illinois regular $3.92 (from $4.23 a week ago), East St. Louis $3.84, Illinois diesel $6.04; Missouri regular $3.36. Level Elevated, trend Rising (market stress).
actions: Don't make panic moves in retirement accounts; avoid new variable-rate debt.
Keep a cash buffer and a few weeks of shelf-stable staples you already eat; don't panic-buy.
Top off vehicles and stored fuel (with stabilizer) while prices are falling.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Space weather
threats.summary: NOAA SWPC Nov 21: no storms now (R0, S0, G0). Next three days: 10% chance of minor and 1% of major radio blackouts, 1% for a solar radiation storm, no geomagnetic storms expected. Level Low, Steady.
actions: No action at G1; G4–G5 would be the point to protect electronics and expect GPS glitches.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Weather: near-record warmth, then rain Sunday and a hard freeze
threats.summary: No NWS alerts for St. Clair County (Nov 21 morning). NWS St. Louis (5:02 AM discussion): one last near-record warm day, sunny and about 72 today. A cold front brings light rain Sunday 7 AM-4 PM (100%, generally 0.25 inch or less; little or no thunder), then colder: low 33 Sunday night with north gusts to 23 mph, high near 50 Monday, low 27 Monday night, 28 Tuesday night; below-normal temperatures and dry most of next week. Level Guarded, Steady.
actions: Before Sunday: disconnect hoses, cover outdoor faucets, check the furnace and bring in sensitive plants.
Stage winter car kits (blanket, water, light, charger) and dress for 20s mornings from Monday.
Check NOAA radio batteries; space heaters need 3 ft clearance and a working CO alarm.
threats.label: official

threats.name: New Madrid seismic zone
threats.summary: USGS: no quake of M1.5 or larger within 300 km of the New Madrid zone since Nov 20 evening (checked Nov 21 morning). Nothing felt locally. Level Low, Steady.
actions: Strap the water heater and anchor tall shelves.
Keep shoes, a flashlight and gloves by each bed.
Know how to shut off gas and water at the house.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Mississippi River flooding
threats.summary: NOAA NWPS: Mississippi at St. Louis 4.4 ft (Nov 21, 6:30 AM), still falling; flood stage 30 ft. Kaskaskia at New Athens 68.5 ft (flood 79); Silver Creek near Mascoutah 8.3 ft. No flood risk; Sunday's light rain won't change that. Level Low, Falling.
actions: No action; recheck if the forecast climbs toward the 28 ft action stage.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Power grid (Ameren Illinois)
threats.summary: Ameren outage data Nov 21, 6:55 AM: 3 Ameren Illinois customers out statewide, 1,467 Ameren Missouri (8 outages); 1 customer out in St. Clair County. MISO status Normal (only routine advisories in the last 72 hours). Level Low, Steady.
actions: Text REG to AMEREN (263736) to get outage alerts.
Keep phones charged and power banks topped up.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Air quality
threats.summary: AirNow St. Louis area: AQI 57 (Moderate, fine particles PM2.5) at 6 AM Nov 21, down from 86 Friday evening; no Action Day. Unusually sensitive people should consider limiting long or heavy outdoor exertion. Sunday's rain should help. Level Guarded, trend Falling.
actions: People with asthma or heart or lung conditions: keep long outdoor exertion short today.
Keep spare HVAC filters (MERV 13) and N95s for smoke days.
Check AirNow before long outdoor activity.
threats.label: official

threats.name: Local crime and public safety
threats.summary: BND's Nov 21 metro-east crime roundup is mostly court action on earlier cases (October Cahokia Heights spa arson indictment, a Swansea stabbing murder charge, an off-duty officer held in an October Belleville shooting) plus the Nov 17-18 Illinois State Police operation (12 arrests, 6 guns) in East St. Louis and nearby communities. No new major public-safety incident found in nearby communities. Level Guarded, Steady.
actions: Lock vehicles and garage overnight; keep exterior lights on.
Agree on a household plan for staying aware and calling home if approached by strangers.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Road and transport safety
threats.summary: A 55-year-old pedestrian was struck and killed in a marked crosswalk on South Green Mount Road at Weatherstone Drive near Belleville on the evening of Nov 18; the driver stayed and no charges have been filed (BND, Nov 19). Thanksgiving travel starts next week. Level Guarded, Steady.
actions: Walk with a light or reflective gear after dark; early sunsets make crosswalks riskier.
Keep winter car kits (blanket, water, light, charger) in each vehicle.
Plan Thanksgiving trips with fuel, weather and a check-in time.
threats.label: verified

threats.name: Regional military and critical infrastructure (public news)
threats.summary: DHS NTAS has no current advisories (Nov 21 morning). Public news about regional military and critical-infrastructure sites remains routine (contracting and event notices); no security incident reported. Level Low, Steady.
actions: Monitor only.
threats.label: assessment

threats.name: Granite City hospital on EMS bypass (Gateway Regional)
threats.summary: Illinois rejected a $9 million emergency-funding request for Gateway Regional Medical Center in Granite City, citing $120 million in unpaid taxes and failed repayment plans (St. Louis Business Journal, Nov 18). The hospital remains on ambulance bypass since Nov 7 over staffing and payroll problems; closure risk is rising but no closure order is reported. Expect longer ambulance trips to other area hospitals. Level Low, trend Rising.
actions: Know your two nearest open ERs and urgent cares (Prep > Help nearby lists them).
Keep a printed med list and insurance card in each go-bag in case you end up at an unfamiliar hospital.
threats.label: verified
